### TAG-212: Runtime: execute `Statement.invoke` (cross-definition invocation), scalar only

**Status:** ✅ Implemented

## Software Notes

`network.zig`'s parser already produces a first-class `Statement.invoke` (an `Invocation` with `name`, `sources`, `destinations`) when one definition calls another from inside its resolution — e.g.:

```
CHAIN[(X0<> X1<> X2<>)($SUM0 $SUM1 $COUT)
  FULLADD($X0 $X1 $X2)(SUM0<> C1<>)
  FULLADD($X0 $X1 $C1)(SUM1<> COUT<>)
]
```

This parses cleanly today (confirmed via parser diagnostics on [TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers)), but `rules.zig`'s own header comment states explicitly: *"No .invoke, no ROM lookup tables, no @generate."* `buildRules` only scans `def.resolution` for `.fill`, so every `.invoke` statement is currently silently ignored — any destination that depends on one stays null forever, with no error.

**Scope**

Add support in `buildRules`/`rules.zig` for executing a `.invoke` statement whose sources and destinations are all plain scalar places (no bundling — that's the separate follow-up ticket [TAG-213](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-213/runtimeparser-bare-name-bundle-aliasing-at-invocation-boundaries) ). For each `.invoke` statement:

1. Look up the named callee definition (`inv.name`) within the network.
2. Build (or reuse a cached build of) the callee's own `ExecutableRule` set.
3. Map the caller's `inv.sources` places to the callee's declared source ports, and the callee's declared destination ports to the caller's `inv.destinations` places.
4. Instantiate the callee's rules against this mapping (either by inlining renamed rules into the caller's rule set, or by running the callee in a sub-`Environment` and copying results back out — open design choice, pick whichever fits `rules.zig`'s existing fixed-point loop most naturally).
5. Ensure repeated invocations of the same callee within one definition (as in `CHAIN` above, which calls `FULLADD` twice) don't collide — each invocation needs its own private internal place names.

**Out of scope**

* Any argument or destination that is a bundle/group (`[...]`) — tracked separately.
* `@generate` and ROM lookup tables — separate, unrelated gaps also noted in `rules.zig`'s header comment.

**Acceptance criteria**

* The full-adder-based `4BITADD` example from [TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers), once its stray colon is removed, is **not** in scope for this ticket (it needs bundling) — but a scalar analog with the colon removed and no bundled ports should pass.
* Regression: existing passing examples ([TAG-143](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-143/example-122-expressing-a-single-return-to-place-of-invocation), [TAG-177](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-177/example-1226-pure-value-expression-of-boolean-full-adder), [TAG-181](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-181/example-1211-controlled-fan-out-expression), [TAG-198](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-198/example-1225-pure-value-expression)) remain unaffected — none of them use `.invoke`.

The emitter fixes (plain-place arguments no longer collapsing to `null_value`, port names resolved against the callee's real ports instead of generic `arg_N`/`output_N`) and the `validate.zig` flat-definition-space enforcement both came directly out of doing this work, not as planned deliverables. I'd credit them here rather than let them go undocumented, even if you'd rather track the flat-definition-space decision as its own retroactive ticket for cleanliness.
